note: SEED SET — starting points for owner curation before execution. Each query needs a filled bench/gold/<id>.json sheet before A1-A5 scoring; the runner reports structure-only metrics otherwise. Query text is public; gold labels are scoring data the pipeline never reads.

queries.query: Why did the WannaCry ransomware worm spread so fast in May 2017?
queries.note: Canonical anchor: the 2026-09-05 showcase sample already ran this and self-disclosed all-medium confidence — a regression/calibration reference for the pilot.

queries.query: In which year and by which country was Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, launched?
queries.note: Closed factual; single well-documented answer reachable by Wikipedia + DuckDuckGo HTML.

queries.query: What distinguishes a comet from an asteroid?
Was the telephone invented by Alexander Graham Bell or by Antonio Meucci?
queries.note: Disagreement class: genuine historical dispute, sources conflict (incl. the 2002 US House resolution on Meucci). Expect the contradiction pass to fire and no confident one-sided high.

queries.query: Was the radio invented by Guglielmo Marconi or by Nikola Tesla?
queries.note: Disagreement class, second D sample (A4 re-spec: the contradiction pass must fire on >= half the paired D queries): Marconi-vs-Tesla priority dispute over radio. Factual anchors = the 1900 Tesla patent grant (No. 645,576) and the 1943 Supreme Court ruling in Marconi Wireless Telegraph Co. of America v. United States; flat one-sided credit claims on both sides are genuinely contested. Mirrors the d1-telephone gold sheet shape.

queries.query: What was the total annual cargo tonnage handled by the port of Trieste in 1928?
queries.note: Deliberately hard/niche: thin, mostly paywalled or archive-only web evidence. Expect unsupported/low or gaps, never confident fabrication.

queries.query: How many steam locomotives were in service on the London Underground in 1905?
queries.note: Hard/niche: obscure statistic, likely thin public evidence; tests honest failure.
